description: Ancient Indian armies made extensive use of iron and, by later periods, high-quality steel arrowheads, taking advantage of the subcontinent’s advanced traditions of ferrous metallurgy. These hardened points could be produced in narrow piercing, broad cutting, or barbed forms and were used by infantry archers, cavalry, and sometimes chariot crews against both lightly and heavily equipped enemies. Their durability and penetrating power made them effective against shields, leather defenses, and vulnerable gaps in armor, while massed archery remained an important feature of Indian warfare from the Mauryan era through later ancient kingdoms.
tooltip: [font="sans-bold-14"]• Archer units +15% attack bonus vs. Cavalry and Elephants.[/font]
